records.literal_gloss: In [the] second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on [the] first day of the month, the word of Yahweh came by [the] hand of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:

en.L: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came by the hand of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
en.B: In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came through the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
en.R: In Darius's second year as king, on the first day of the sixth month of the year, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave a message through the prophet Haggai. It was for Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.

fr.L: La deuxième année de Darius le roi, le sixième mois, le premier jour du mois, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée par la main d’Aggée le prophète à Zorobabel fils de Salathiel, gouverneur de Juda, et à Josué fils de Yehotsadaq, le grand prêtre, disant :
fr.B: La deuxième année du règne de Darius, le sixième mois, le premier jour du mois, la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée par le prophète Aggée à Zorobabel fils de Salathiel, gouverneur de Juda, et à Josué fils de Yehotsadaq, le grand prêtre :
fr.R: La deuxième année où Darius était roi, le premier jour du sixième mois de l’année, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un message par l’intermédiaire du prophète Aggée. Ce message était pour Zorobabel fils de Salathiel, gouverneur de Juda, et pour Josué fils de Yehotsadaq, le grand prêtre.

es.L: En el año segundo del rey Darío, en el mes sexto, el día primero del mes, vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} por medio del profeta Hageo a Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel, gobernador de Judá, y a Josué hijo de Josadac, el sumo sacerdote, diciendo:
es.B: En el segundo año del reinado de Darío, en el mes sexto, el día primero del mes, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino por medio del profeta Hageo a Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel, gobernador de Judá, y a Josué hijo de Josadac, el sumo sacerdote:
es.R: En el segundo año de Darío como rey, el primer día del sexto mes del año, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dio un mensaje por medio del profeta Hageo. Era para Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel, gobernador de Judá, y para Josué hijo de Josadac, el sumo sacerdote.

sw.L: Katika mwaka wa pili wa mfalme Dario, mwezi wa sita, siku ya kwanza ya mwezi, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilikuja kwa mkono wa Hagai nabii kwa Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli, liwali wa Yuda, na kwa Yoshua mwana wa Yehosadaki, kuhani mkuu, kusema:
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa pili wa utawala wa Dario, mwezi wa sita, siku ya kwanza ya mwezi, neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilikuja kupitia nabii Hagai kwa Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli, liwali wa Yuda, na kwa Yoshua mwana wa Yehosadaki, kuhani mkuu:
sw.R: Katika mwaka wa pili wa Dario kuwa mfalme, siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa sita wa mwaka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitoa ujumbe kupitia nabii Hagai. Ujumbe huo ulikuwa kwa ajili ya Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli, liwali wa Yuda, na Yoshua mwana wa Yehosadaki, kuhani mkuu.

vi.L: Năm thứ hai đời vua Đa-ri-út, tháng thứ sáu, ngày mồng một trong tháng, lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến qua tay A-ghê, nhà tiên tri, cho Xô-rô-ba-bên con trai Sa-la-thi-ên, tổng đốc Giu-đa, và cho Giô-suê con trai Giê-hô-xa-đác, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm, rằng:
vi.B: Ngày mồng một tháng sáu, năm thứ hai triều vua Đa-ri-út, lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến qua nhà tiên tri A-ghê cho Xô-rô-ba-bên con trai Sa-la-thi-ên, tổng đốc Giu-đa, và Giô-suê con trai Giê-hô-xa-đác, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm:
vi.R: Ngày mồng một tháng sáu, năm thứ hai Đa-ri-út làm vua, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban một sứ điệp qua nhà tiên tri A-ghê. Sứ điệp ấy dành cho Xô-rô-ba-bên con trai Sa-la-thi-ên, tổng đốc Giu-đa, và Giô-suê con trai Giê-hô-xa-đác, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm.

ko.L: 다리오 왕 제2년 여섯째 달, 그달 초하루에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 예언자 학개의 손을 통하여 유다 총독 스알디엘의 아들 스룹바벨과 여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아에게 임하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 다리오가 다스린 지 2년째 되는 해 여섯째 달 초하루에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 예언자 학개를 통하여 유다 총독 스알디엘의 아들 스룹바벨과 여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아에게 임했다.
ko.R: 다리오가 왕이 된 지 2년째 되는 해 여섯째 달 1일에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 예언자 학개를 통하여 말씀을 주셨다. 그 말씀은 유다 총독인 스알디엘의 아들 스룹바벨과 여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아에게 주신 것이었다.

pt.L: No segundo ano do rei Dario, no sexto mês, no primeiro dia do mês, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio pela mão de Ageu, o profeta, a Zorobabel, filho de Salatiel, governador de Judá, e a Josué, filho de Jeozadaque, o sumo sacerdote, dizendo:
pt.B: No segundo ano do rei Dario, no sexto mês, no primeiro dia do mês, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio por meio do profeta Ageu a Zorobabel, filho de Salatiel, governador de Judá, e a Josué, filho de Jeozadaque, o sumo sacerdote:
pt.R: No dia primeiro do sexto mês do ano, no segundo ano em que Dario era rei, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu uma mensagem por meio do profeta Ageu. Ela era para Zorobabel, filho de Salatiel, governador de Judá, e para Josué, filho de Jeozadaque, o sumo sacerdote.

decisions.choice: the second year of King Darius, the sixth month, the first day: late August 520 BC
decisions.reason: Darius I ruled the Persian empire from 522 to 486 BC, so his second year was 520 BC. The months are counted from the spring, and the first day of the sixth month (Elul) fell on about 29 August 520 BC. The first day of a month, the new moon, was a day when people gathered for worship (Isaiah 66:23; Amos 8:5), so the prophet had a crowd to hear him. Haggai dates each of his messages; all four fall within four months of that year. |

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Jehozadak: the same man as "Jeshua son of Jozadak" in Ezra
decisions.reason: Haggai and Zechariah use the full form of the high priest's name, Joshua, and of his father's, Jehozadak. Ezra and Nehemiah use the later short forms, Jeshua and Jozadak (Ezra 3:2; 5:2), for the same man. Jehozadak was the priest taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar (1 Chronicles 5:40-41 in the Hebrew numbering, 6:14-15 in many other Bibles), so Joshua was born in exile and returned with Zerubbabel. Each book keeps the form of the name its own text uses. |

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel was a grandson of King Jehoiachin, who was taken to Babylon in 597 BC (1 Chronicles 3:17-19, which names his father as Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother; Ezra 3:2 and Haggai call him son of Shealtiel). He led a group of exiles home (Ezra 2:2) and served as governor of Judah, then a small province of the Persian empire. He is named in the family line of Jesus (Matthew 1:12; Luke 3:27). |

decisions.choice: by the hand of Haggai: through Haggai
decisions.reason: The word of the LORD came "by the hand of" the prophet: he was the one through whom it was given. Haggai is known otherwise only from Ezra 5:1 and 6:14, where he and Zechariah urge the people to rebuild the temple. |

decisions.choice: the date in the Hebrew form at every level; in the second year of Darius the king (L), of King Darius (B), in Darius's second year as king (R)
decisions.reason: Haggai's dates keep their Hebrew form, as set for the Twelve; the modern date is given in m1, not in the text. Readable says "the sixth month of the year" and follows the Jeremiah table for "the Nth year of X". |

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest
decisions.reason: The two leaders are named the same way at every level and in every verse of Haggai where the Hebrew names them so (1:12, 14; 2:2, 4). "The high priest" is the usual English for "the great priest". Balanced and Readable drop the second "to"; Readable splits the heading into two sentences. Haggai is prose: dated reports of the prophet's messages and of what the people did. |

decisions.choice: Haggai's narrative frames (1:1, 3, 12-15; 2:1, 10, 20) in the passé simple at L and B and the passé composé at R; the LORD's words are speech
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the dated reports are narrative, the oracles speech.

decisions.choice: Dates "la deuxième année de Darius le roi" (L), "du règne de Darius" (B), "où Darius était roi" (R), no modern calendar; "par la main d'Aggée" (L), "par le prophète Aggée" (B, R); "Josué fils de Yehotsadaq" in Haggai and Zechariah
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms. The high priest keeps the Hebrew form of these books, "Josué fils de Yehotsadaq"; Ezra's "Yeshoua fils de Yotsadaq" is the same man, as the English meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "en el año segundo del rey Darío, en el mes sexto, el día primero del mes" (L); "en el segundo año del reinado de Darío" (B); "en el segundo año de Darío como rey, el primer día del sexto mes del año" (R)
decisions.reason: The dates of Haggai and Zechariah keep the Hebrew form at each level, as the term sheet sets; none is turned into a modern date in the text.

decisions.choice: "por medio del profeta Hageo"; "Josué hijo de Josadac"
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" is said "por medio de" at every level, since "por mano de" reads oddly in Spanish. The high priest is "Josué" in Haggai and Zechariah, as the Hebrew writes him, and "Jesúa" in Ezra; Zorobabel, Salatiel, Darío and Hageo are the published forms.

decisions.choice: "katika mwaka wa pili wa mfalme Dario" (L); "wa utawala wa Dario" (B); "wa Dario kuwa mfalme" (R); the Hebrew form of the date at every level
decisions.reason: The dated headings of Haggai and Zechariah follow the term sheet and Jeremiah; Readable says "mwezi wa sita wa mwaka" but does not convert to a modern calendar. Recorded once for Haggai and Zechariah.

decisions.choice: "Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli, liwali wa Yuda"; "Yoshua mwana wa Yehosadaki, kuhani mkuu"
decisions.reason: The high priest keeps Haggai's long form, "Yoshua mwana wa Yehosadaki" (as 1 Chronicles 5:40), while Ezra calls the same man "Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki"; the English culture decision links the two. "Liwali" is the governor, as 2 Kings 18:24 and Ezra.

decisions.choice: the dated heading in the terms note's forms: Hebrew order at L ("Năm thứ hai đời vua Đa-ri-út, tháng thứ sáu, ngày mồng một trong tháng"); "ngày mồng một tháng sáu, năm thứ hai triều vua Đa-ri-út" (B); "... năm thứ hai Đa-ri-út làm vua" (R)
decisions.reason: No level converts to a modern date; the culture decision gives it. Book-wide for Haggai and Zechariah: "the LORD of hosts" is "CHÚA Vạn Quân" with the span on CHÚA; "Thus says" is "phán thế này:" (L) / "phán như vầy:" (B) / "Đây là lời ... phán:" (R); 'amar YHWH is "CHÚA phán" and ne'um YHWH "CHÚA phán vậy" (L, B) / "CHÚA phán" (R); God speaks to the people as "các ngươi"; the temple is "nhà" (L, B) / "đền thờ" (R).

decisions.choice: "Giô-suê con trai Giê-hô-xa-đác", with "Xô-rô-ba-bên con trai Sa-la-thi-ên" as in Matthew 1:12
decisions.reason: The terms note: the English "Joshua" is the same Hebrew name as Moses' successor, so his form is used; Ezra's short form is "Giê-sua con trai Giô-xa-đác" and the culture decision links the two men. The 1926 form is "Giê-hô-sua".

decisions.choice: Dated headings follow the Kings formula: "다리오 왕 제2년 여섯째 달 … 초하루에" (L), "다리오가 다스린 지 2년째 되는 해 여섯째 달 초하루에" (B), "다리오가 왕이 된 지 2년째 되는 해 여섯째 달 1일에" (R); months and days in words at L and B, years in figures
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the dated headings of Haggai and Zechariah (2 Kings 25:1); the culture decision gives the modern date. Recorded once for Haggai and Zechariah.

decisions.choice: "유다 총독 스알디엘의 아들 스룹바벨" and "여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아"
decisions.reason: Haggai and Zechariah have the long Hebrew forms of the high priest's name, written as 1 Chronicles 5:40 ("여호사닥") and as Moses' successor ("여호수아"); Ezra's short forms are "요사닥의 아들 예수아". He is the same man, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: no segundo ano do rei Dario, no sexto mês, no primeiro dia do mês (L, B); no dia primeiro do sexto mês do ano, no segundo ano em que Dario era rei (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (1:15; 2:1, 10, 18, 20): the dates keep one formula at each level, with ordinals in words, as Zechariah 1:1 and 1:7 give the same king's dates in Portuguese; Readable says the day as Brazilians say dates ("no dia primeiro", "no dia vinte e quatro") and "em que Dario era rei", as Zechariah's Readable does. "Ageu, o profeta" (L) is the form of Ezra 5:1 and 6:14.

decisions.choice: Zorobabel, filho de Salatiel, governador de Judá; Josué, filho de Jeozadaque, o sumo sacerdote
decisions.reason: For the whole book, at every level and in every verse that names them (1:12, 14; 2:2, 4, 21, 23): Zerubbabel and his father keep the forms of Ezra 3:2 and 5:2 in Portuguese, "Zorobabel, filho de Salatiel". The high priest has the long forms here (m2), so he is "Josué", as the Pentateuch writes the name, and his father "Jeozadaque", the long form 1 Chronicles 5:40-41 uses; Ezra's "Jesua, filho de Jozadaque" is the same man.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹ֥א עֶת־בֹּ֛א עֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה לְהִבָּנֽוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, saying: This people have said, [It is] not [the] time to come, [the] time [for the] house of Yahweh to be rebuilt.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: This people says, "The time has not come, the time for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to be rebuilt."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: These people are saying, "The time has not come, the time to rebuild {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house."
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: The people say, "It is not yet time to build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} again."

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Ce peuple dit : « Le temps n’est pas venu, le temps que la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} soit rebâtie. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Ces gens disent : « Le temps n’est pas venu, le temps de rebâtir la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Le peuple dit : « Ce n’est pas encore le moment de reconstruire le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: Este pueblo dice: «No ha llegado el tiempo, el tiempo de que la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sea reedificada».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: Este pueblo anda diciendo: «No ha llegado el tiempo, el tiempo de reconstruir la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: La gente dice: «Todavía no es tiempo de volver a construir el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Watu hawa wanasema, "Wakati haujafika, wakati wa nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kujengwa upya."
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Watu hawa wanasema, "Wakati haujafika, wakati wa kuijenga upya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Watu wanasema, "Bado si wakati wa kulijenga upya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Dân này nói: "Chưa đến lúc, lúc để nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} được xây lại."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Dân này nói: "Chưa đến lúc, chưa đến lúc xây lại nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Dân chúng nói: "Chưa phải lúc xây lại đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 이 백성이 "때가 오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집을 다시 지을 때가 [오지 않았다]" 하고 말한다.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 이 백성이 "아직 때가 오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집을 다시 지을 때가 오지 않았다" 하고 말하고 있다.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 백성이 "아직은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 다시 지을 때가 아니다" 하고 말한다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Este povo diz: "Não chegou o tempo, o tempo de a casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} ser reconstruída."
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Este povo anda dizendo: "Ainda não chegou o tempo, o tempo de reconstruir a casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}."
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos diz: O povo diz: "Ainda não é hora de construir de novo o templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}."

decisions.choice: this people: said with distance, not "my people"
decisions.reason: The LORD does not call them "my people" here. The same phrase shows his displeasure in Isaiah 6:9-10 and Jeremiah 14:10-11. |

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the temple in Jerusalem, still in ruins
decisions.reason: Solomon's temple was destroyed by the Babylonians in 587 BC (2 Kings 25:9). Exiles returned after Cyrus's decree of 538 BC and laid a foundation, but opposition from their neighbors stopped the work (Ezra 3:8-4:5, 24). Sixteen years or more later it still lay in ruins, and the people said the right time had not come. |

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L), The LORD of Armies says this (B), This is what the LORD of Armies says (R); house (L, B), temple (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the Isaiah table. Literal and Balanced keep "house", which Haggai sets against the people's own houses (verses 4 and 9); Readable says "temple" so that the reader knows which building is meant, and the contrast is carried by "your own houses". |

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR des armées :" (L), "Le SEIGNEUR des armées dit ceci :" (B), "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR des armées :" (R), "des armées" at every level
alternatives: "le SEIGNEUR des Armées" at B and R
decisions.reason: The French prophets' formula; French keeps "des armées" where the English Balanced and Readable say "of Armies".

decisions.choice: "Así dice el SEÑOR de los ejércitos:" (L); "El SEÑOR de los Ejércitos dice esto:" (B); "Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR de los Ejércitos:" (R)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula and the title follow the Spanish prophets at each level; God's words take no quotation marks, and the people's words inside them take « ».

decisions.choice: "BWANA wa majeshi asema hivi:" (L); "Hivi ndivyo BWANA wa majeshi asemavyo:" (B); "Hili ndilo BWANA wa majeshi analosema:" (R)
decisions.reason: "Thus says the LORD" as the Isaiah block and 2 Kings 19:6 set it, with "BWANA wa majeshi" at every level. God's words that follow take no quotation marks; the people's words quoted in them take double quotes. Recorded once for Haggai and Zechariah.

decisions.choice: "nyumba ya BWANA" (L, B); "hekalu la BWANA" (R)
decisions.reason: The house of the LORD is the temple; L and B keep "nyumba", Readable names it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "dân này", not "dân Ta"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: God speaks of them with distance; Vietnamese "dân này" keeps it.

decisions.choice: "Thus says the LORD of hosts" is "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L), "…이렇게 말씀하신다" (B), "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다" (R), ending in a period
decisions.reason: The formula as Isaiah and Jeremiah settled it in Korean; it keeps "께서" even inside God's message. Through Haggai and Zechariah.

decisions.choice: Assim diz o SENHOR dos Exércitos (L, B); É isto que o SENHOR dos Exércitos diz (R); a casa (L, B), o templo (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the messenger formula as Isaiah and Jeremiah set it at each level, and YHWH Tsevaot "o SENHOR dos Exércitos" at every level where the English Balanced says "of Armies". Literal and Balanced keep "casa", which Haggai sets against the people's own houses (verses 4, 9); Readable says "templo".

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came: the LORD's answer to what the people said
decisions.reason: The heading introduces the LORD's reply to the people's excuse in verse 2. "By the hand of" means through, as in verse 1. |

decisions.choice: came by the hand of (L), came through (B), gave this message through (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows verse 1 at each level. |

decisions.reason: "By the hand of" is kept word for word at L and means "through", which B and R say.

decisions.choice: "qua tay" kept at Literal
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: "by the hand of" means "through"; Literal keeps the Hebrew image, Balanced and Readable say "qua".

decisions.choice: "the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai, saying" is "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 … 학개의 손을 통하여 임하여 말씀하셨다" (L), "…학개를 통하여 임했다" (B), "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 … 학개를 통하여 이 말씀을 주셨다" (R)

source.text: הַעֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אַתֶּ֔ם לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֣ם סְפוּנִ֑ים וְהַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה חָרֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house [lies] desolate?

en.L: Is it a time for you, you yourselves, to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house [is] desolate?
en.B: Is it a time for you yourselves to live in paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
en.R: Is it the right time for you to live in fine houses with wood-paneled walls, while this temple is still in ruins?

fr.L: Est-ce le temps pour vous, vous-mêmes, d’habiter dans vos maisons lambrissées, tandis que cette maison [est] dévastée ?
fr.B: Est-ce bien le moment pour vous d’habiter des maisons lambrissées, alors que cette maison est en ruines ?
fr.R: Est-ce vraiment le moment pour vous d’habiter de belles maisons aux murs couverts de bois, alors que ce temple est toujours en ruines ?

es.L: ¿Es tiempo para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos, de habitar en {{plural_you:sus casas|vuestras casas}} artesonadas, mientras esta casa [está] desolada?
es.B: ¿Es tiempo de que {{plural_you:ustedes mismos vivan|vosotros mismos viváis}} en casas con paneles de madera, mientras esta casa está en ruinas?
es.R: ¿{{plural_you:Les|Os}} parece que es el momento de vivir en casas lujosas con paredes de madera fina, mientras este templo sigue en ruinas?

sw.L: Je, ni wakati kwenu, ninyi wenyewe, kukaa katika nyumba zenu zilizopambwa kwa mbao, na nyumba hii [ni] ukiwa?
sw.B: Je, ni wakati kwenu ninyi wenyewe kuishi katika nyumba zilizopambwa kwa mbao, wakati nyumba hii imebaki magofu?
sw.R: Je, ni wakati unaofaa kwenu kuishi katika nyumba nzuri zenye kuta zilizopambwa kwa mbao, wakati hekalu hili bado ni magofu?

vi.L: Có phải là lúc cho các ngươi, chính các ngươi, ở trong những ngôi nhà ốp gỗ của mình, trong khi nhà này [bị] hoang tàn?
vi.B: Có phải đây là lúc chính các ngươi được ở trong những ngôi nhà ốp gỗ, trong khi nhà này còn đổ nát sao?
vi.R: Bây giờ có phải là lúc các ngươi sống trong những ngôi nhà đẹp đẽ có tường ốp gỗ, trong khi đền thờ này vẫn còn đổ nát không?

ko.L: 이 집이 황폐한데, 너희, 너희 자신이 판자로 꾸민 너희 집들에 살 때이냐?
ko.B: 이 집은 폐허로 버려져 있는데, 너희는 판자로 잘 꾸민 집에서 살고 있을 때냐?
ko.R: 이 성전은 아직도 무너진 채로 있는데, 너희가 나무판자로 벽을 꾸민 좋은 집에서 살고 있을 때냐?

pt.L: [É] tempo de vocês, vocês mesmos, habitarem nas suas casas forradas, enquanto esta casa [está] desolada?
pt.B: Será que é tempo de vocês mesmos morarem em casas forradas de madeira, enquanto esta casa está em ruínas?
pt.R: Será que agora é a hora certa de vocês morarem em casas bonitas, com paredes revestidas de madeira, enquanto este templo continua em ruínas?

decisions.choice: is it a time for you: a reply to "the time has not come"
decisions.reason: The people said the time had not come for the LORD's house (verse 2). The LORD asks whether it is the time for their own fine houses. "You yourselves" is emphatic. |

decisions.choice: paneled houses: houses lined or roofed with wood
decisions.reason: The word is used of the cedar paneling of Solomon's temple and palace (1 Kings 6:9; 7:3, 7) and of a king's luxurious house (Jeremiah 22:14). It may mean walls lined with wood or simply roofed. Either way the people have homes finished and comfortable, while the LORD's house lies open.

decisions.choice: desolate: in ruins, dry and waste
decisions.reason: The word means "dry, laid waste". It sounds like the word for "drought" in verse 11, which is the LORD's answer: their land will be as dry as his house is waste. |

decisions.choice: fine houses with wood-paneled walls (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what paneled houses were (m2). |

decisions.choice: plural_you throughout Haggai's speeches to the people
decisions.reason: The people are addressed as a group, so every plural "you" in Haggai takes the plural_you setting.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת שִׂ֥ימוּ לְבַבְכֶ֖ם עַל־דַּרְכֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, thus says Yahweh of hosts: Set your heart on your ways.

en.L: And now, thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Set your heart on your ways.
en.B: So now, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Think carefully about how you are living.
en.R: Now this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Think carefully about the way you have been living and what it has brought you.

fr.L: Et maintenant, ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Mettez votre cœur sur vos chemins.
fr.B: Maintenant donc, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Réfléchissez bien à votre manière de vivre.
fr.R: Maintenant, voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Réfléchissez bien à la manière dont vous vivez et à ce qu’elle vous a apporté.

es.L: Y ahora, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: {{plural_you:Pongan su corazón|Poned vuestro corazón}} en {{plural_you:sus caminos|vuestros caminos}}.
es.B: Así que ahora, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} bien en cómo {{plural_you:están viviendo|estáis viviendo}}.
es.R: Ahora bien, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} bien en la forma en que {{plural_you:han vivido|habéis vivido}} y en lo que eso {{plural_you:les|os}} ha traído.

sw.L: Basi sasa, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Wekeni mioyo yenu juu ya njia zenu.
sw.B: Basi sasa, hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Fikirini kwa makini jinsi mnavyoishi.
sw.R: Sasa, hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Fikirini kwa makini jinsi mlivyokuwa mkiishi na matokeo yake.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Hãy để lòng các ngươi vào đường lối các ngươi.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Hãy suy xét kỹ cách các ngươi đang sống.
vi.R: Bây giờ, đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Hãy suy nghĩ kỹ về cách các ngươi đã sống và những gì điều đó mang lại cho các ngươi.

ko.L: 그러므로 이제 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 너희의 길에 너희의 마음을 두어라.
ko.B: 그러므로 이제 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 너희가 어떻게 살고 있는지 깊이 생각해 보아라.
ko.R: 이제 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 너희가 지금까지 어떻게 살아왔고, 그 결과가 어떠했는지 잘 생각해 보아라.

pt.L: E agora, assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Ponham o coração nos seus caminhos.
pt.B: Agora, pois, assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Considerem os seus caminhos.
pt.R: Agora, é isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos diz: Pensem bem no modo como vocês têm vivido e no que isso trouxe para vocês.

decisions.choice: set your heart on your ways: think carefully about what you are doing and what has come of it
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought, so to "set the heart on" something is to give it careful thought. "Your ways" are their conduct, and the results it brings, which verse 6 lists. Haggai repeats the call in verse 7 and in 2:15 and 2:18. |

decisions.choice: Think carefully about how you are living (B); the way you have been living and what it has brought you (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1). Readable adds "what it has brought you" because verse 6 goes on to list the results. The same wording is used in verse 7. |

decisions.choice: "Set your heart on your ways" is "너희의 길에 너희의 마음을 두어라" (L), "어떻게 살고 있는지 깊이 생각해 보아라" (B), "…그 결과가 어떠했는지 잘 생각해 보아라" (R), worded the same in 1:7
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable say its meaning, as the English does, and the refrain keeps one wording at each level.

decisions.choice: Ponham o coração nos seus caminhos (L); Considerem os seus caminhos (B); Pensem bem no modo como vocês têm vivido (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Haggai's repeated call (m1) has one wording at each level, the same in verse 7, and with "ponham o coração" (L), "considerem" (B) and "pensem bem" (R) in 2:15 and 2:18. Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced keeps the short call with "caminhos" for the people's conduct; Readable says what it means, as the English does.

source.text: זְרַעְתֶּ֨ם הַרְבֵּ֜ה וְהָבֵ֣א מְעָ֗ט אָכ֤וֹל וְאֵין־לְשָׂבְעָה֙ שָׁת֣וֹ וְאֵין־לְשָׁכְרָ֔ה לָב֖וֹשׁ וְאֵין־לְחֹ֣ם ל֑וֹ וְהַ֨מִּשְׂתַּכֵּ֔ר מִשְׂתַּכֵּ֖ר אֶל־צְר֥וֹר נָקֽוּב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: You have sown much and brought in little; eating, but there is no satisfying; drinking, but there is no drunkenness; clothing [yourselves], but there is no warmth to him; and the one earning wages earns wages into a bag pierced.

en.L: You have sown much and brought in little; eating, but not to be satisfied; drinking, but not to be filled; putting on clothes, but no one is warm; and the one who earns wages earns wages for a bag with holes.
en.B: You have sown much and harvested little. You eat, yet are never satisfied; you drink, yet never have your fill; you dress, yet no one is warm. And whoever earns wages earns them only to put them in a purse with holes.
en.R: You have planted a lot of seed, but you have harvested very little. You eat, but you are still hungry. You drink, but you are still thirsty. You put on clothes, but you are not warm. The money you earn disappears, as if you put it in a bag with holes in it.

fr.L: Vous avez semé beaucoup et rentré peu ; [vous] mangez, mais sans être rassasiés ; [vous] buvez, mais sans être désaltérés ; [vous] vous habillez, mais personne n’a chaud ; et celui qui gagne un salaire gagne un salaire pour une bourse percée.
fr.B: Vous avez semé beaucoup et récolté peu. Vous mangez, mais vous n’êtes jamais rassasiés ; vous buvez, mais vous n’avez jamais assez ; vous vous habillez, mais personne n’a chaud. Et celui qui gagne un salaire le gagne pour le mettre dans une bourse trouée.
fr.R: Vous avez planté beaucoup de semences, mais vous avez très peu récolté. Vous mangez, mais vous avez encore faim. Vous buvez, mais vous avez encore soif. Vous mettez des vêtements, mais vous n’avez pas chaud. L’argent que vous gagnez disparaît, comme si vous le mettiez dans un sac troué.

es.L: {{plural_you:Han sembrado|Habéis sembrado}} mucho y {{plural_you:han recogido|habéis recogido}} poco; comer, pero sin saciarse; beber, pero sin llegar a llenarse; vestirse, pero nadie entra en calor; y el que gana jornal, gana jornal para una bolsa rota.
es.B: {{plural_you:Han sembrado|Habéis sembrado}} mucho y {{plural_you:han cosechado|habéis cosechado}} poco. {{plural_you:Comen|Coméis}}, pero nunca {{plural_you:quedan|quedáis}} satisfechos; {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}}, pero nunca {{plural_you:se sacian|os saciáis}}; {{plural_you:se visten|os vestís}}, pero nadie entra en calor. Y el que gana un salario lo gana solo para echarlo en una bolsa rota.
es.R: {{plural_you:Han sembrado|Habéis sembrado}} mucha semilla, pero {{plural_you:han cosechado|habéis cosechado}} muy poco. {{plural_you:Comen|Coméis}}, pero {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} con hambre. {{plural_you:Beben|Bebéis}}, pero {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} con sed. {{plural_you:Se ponen|Os ponéis}} ropa, pero no {{plural_you:se calientan|os calentáis}}. El dinero que {{plural_you:ganan|ganáis}} desaparece, como si lo {{plural_you:echaran|echarais}} en una bolsa con agujeros.

sw.L: Mmepanda mbegu nyingi na kuvuna kidogo; mnakula, lakini hamshibi; mnakunywa, lakini hamtosheki; mnavaa nguo, lakini hakuna aliye na joto; na yeye anayepata mshahara anapata mshahara kwa ajili ya mfuko uliotobolewa.
sw.B: Mmepanda mbegu nyingi na kuvuna kidogo. Mnakula, lakini hamshibi kamwe; mnakunywa, lakini hamtosheki kamwe; mnavaa nguo, lakini hakuna aliye na joto. Na kila anayepata mshahara anaupata tu ili kuutia katika mfuko wenye matundu.
sw.R: Mmepanda mbegu nyingi, lakini mmevuna kidogo sana. Mnakula, lakini bado mna njaa. Mnakunywa, lakini bado mna kiu. Mnavaa nguo, lakini hamsikii joto. Pesa mnazopata zinatoweka, kana kwamba mmeziweka katika mfuko wenye matundu.

vi.L: Các ngươi đã gieo nhiều mà thu vào ít; ăn mà không no; uống mà không đã; mặc áo mà không ai ấm; và kẻ làm thuê lãnh tiền công để bỏ vào túi thủng.
vi.B: Các ngươi gieo nhiều mà gặt ít. Các ngươi ăn mà chẳng bao giờ no; uống mà chẳng bao giờ đã khát; mặc áo mà chẳng ai được ấm. Còn ai làm thuê lãnh lương thì chỉ để bỏ vào cái túi thủng.
vi.R: Các ngươi đã gieo nhiều hạt giống, nhưng gặt được rất ít. Các ngươi ăn, nhưng vẫn đói. Các ngươi uống, nhưng vẫn khát. Các ngươi mặc áo, nhưng vẫn không ấm. Tiền các ngươi kiếm được biến mất, như thể các ngươi bỏ nó vào một cái túi thủng.

ko.L: 너희가 많이 뿌렸으나 적게 거두었다. 먹어도 배부르지 않고, 마셔도 흡족하지 않으며, 입어도 따뜻한 사람이 없다. 품삯을 버는 자는 구멍 난 주머니에 넣으려고 품삯을 번다.
ko.B: 너희는 많이 뿌렸지만 적게 거두었다. 먹어도 배부르지 않고, 마셔도 흡족하지 않으며, 옷을 입어도 따뜻하지 않다. 품삯을 받아도 구멍 난 주머니에 넣는 꼴이 된다.
ko.R: 너희는 씨를 많이 뿌렸지만 거둔 것은 아주 적다. 먹어도 여전히 배가 고프다. 마셔도 여전히 목이 마르다. 옷을 입어도 따뜻하지 않다. 돈을 벌어도 구멍 난 주머니에 넣은 것처럼 다 없어진다.

pt.L: Vocês semearam muito e recolheram pouco; comer, mas não para se fartar; beber, mas não para se saciar; vestir-se, mas ninguém se aquece; e o que ganha salário ganha salário para um saco furado.
pt.B: Vocês semearam muito e colheram pouco. Comem, mas nunca ficam satisfeitos; bebem, mas nunca bebem o bastante; vestem-se, mas ninguém se aquece. E quem ganha salário ganha só para pôr numa bolsa furada.
pt.R: Vocês plantaram muita semente, mas colheram muito pouco. Vocês comem, mas continuam com fome. Bebem, mas continuam com sede. Vestem roupas, mas não se aquecem. O dinheiro que vocês ganham desaparece, como se fosse posto num saco furado.

decisions.choice: sown much, brought in little: the curses of the covenant
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:38-40 and Leviticus 26:20, 26 warn that a disobedient people will sow much and gather little, and eat without being satisfied. Hosea 4:10 and Micah 6:14-15 use the same pattern. Haggai's hearers are living under these curses. |

decisions.choice: drinking, but not to be filled: there is not enough to drink one's fill
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "be drunk", but here, beside "eat and not be satisfied", it means drinking as much as one wants (compare Song of Songs 5:1). The point is shortage, not drunkenness. |

decisions.choice: wages into a bag with holes: earnings that vanish as soon as they are earned
decisions.reason: Silver was kept in a cloth bag or purse. With poor harvests, prices were high and wages ran out at once, as if the purse had holes. |

decisions.choice: not to be filled (L), never have your fill (B), still thirsty (R)
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense of the verb here (m2), so that no level speaks of drunkenness. Literal keeps the short Hebrew phrases without verbs ("eating, but not to be satisfied"). |

decisions.choice: infinitives "comer ... beber ... vestirse"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses infinitives after the first clause; Spanish L keeps them, as the English L keeps its "-ing" forms; B and R use finite verbs with plural_you.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת שִׂ֥ימוּ לְבַבְכֶ֖ם עַל־דַּרְכֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Set your heart on your ways.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Set your heart on your ways.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Think carefully about how you are living.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Think carefully about the way you have been living and what it has brought you.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Mettez votre cœur sur vos chemins.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Réfléchissez bien à votre manière de vivre.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Réfléchissez bien à la manière dont vous vivez et à ce qu’elle vous a apporté.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: {{plural_you:Pongan su corazón|Poned vuestro corazón}} en {{plural_you:sus caminos|vuestros caminos}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} bien en cómo {{plural_you:están viviendo|estáis viviendo}}.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} bien en la forma en que {{plural_you:han vivido|habéis vivido}} y en lo que eso {{plural_you:les|os}} ha traído.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Wekeni mioyo yenu juu ya njia zenu.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Fikirini kwa makini jinsi mnavyoishi.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Fikirini kwa makini jinsi mlivyokuwa mkiishi na matokeo yake.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Hãy để lòng các ngươi vào đường lối các ngươi.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Hãy suy xét kỹ cách các ngươi đang sống.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Hãy suy nghĩ kỹ về cách các ngươi đã sống và những gì điều đó mang lại cho các ngươi.

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 너희의 길에 너희의 마음을 두어라.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 너희가 어떻게 살고 있는지 깊이 생각해 보아라.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 너희가 지금까지 어떻게 살아왔고, 그 결과가 어떠했는지 잘 생각해 보아라.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Ponham o coração nos seus caminhos.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Considerem os seus caminhos.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos diz: Pensem bem no modo como vocês têm vivido e no que isso trouxe para vocês.

decisions.reason: Verse 5 used these words to point back to the people's hardships. Here they lead into what the people must now do. |

decisions.choice: the wording of verse 5 at each level
decisions.reason: The repeated call keeps the wording of verse 5 at each level. |

decisions.reason: The call is repeated word for word from verse 5, and the Spanish keeps the same words.
